problem: Traditional path planners struggle in complex semantic environments, while pure LLM planners hallucinate and are logically inconsistent in long-horizon decision-making.
motivation: Embodied agents in unstructured environments need robust long-range decisions under sparse rewards. LLM commonsense priors can narrow the search space, while look-ahead search can correct LLM inconsistency.
key_idea: Use LLM-generated commonsense action priors to guide Deep MCTS, together with a semantic consistency value function and entropy-based dynamic pruning.
insight: The abstract says the LLM priors shrink MCTS search width and the search corrects LLM hallucination, so the two components complement each other. It reports 74.2% success, 35.3% above pure LLM planning, and a 40.4% reduction in average search depth. Ablations are not available in the abstract only.
method: LLM action prior: generates commonsense-based high-confidence action priors that reduce MCTS search width
Deep MCTS: look-ahead tree search guided by the priors, addressing sparse-reward exploration
Semantic consistency value function: scores states by semantic consistency to give a value signal
Entropy-based dynamic pruning: prunes search branches according to entropy to reduce search depth and cost

setting.backbone: LLM (unspecified) + deep MCTS with learned value function
setting.simulator: not specified (high-fidelity semantic navigation environment; NVIDIA H800 cluster)

numbers_note: abstract only; the 74.2% success rate is reported without benchmark, split, or full metrics, so no per-benchmark entry is created
results: SA-MCTS reaches 74.2% success in complex tasks, 35.3% above the pure LLM planning method. It also reduces average search depth by 40.4%.
limitations: Only the abstract is available; benchmark, baselines, and ablations are unspecified
Evaluation appears to be in simulation only, with heavy compute (H800 cluster)
